title: Shoes on, shoes off
setting: A Saturday morning at the front door. Yuki is taking her little brother Kenji shopping, and he is slowly getting ready.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenji, kaimono iku yo! fuku kita?
lines.ja: ケンジ、買い物行くよ！服着た？
lines.kana: けんじ、かいものいくよ！ふくきた？
lines.english: Kenji, we're going shopping! Are you dressed?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: kiteru yo. ima kutsu haku kara.
lines.ja: 着てるよ。今靴履くから。
lines.kana: きてるよ。いまくつはくから。
lines.english: I'm dressed. I'm just putting my shoes on.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: watashi wa mou kutsu haiteru yo.
lines.ja: 私はもう靴履いてるよ。
lines.kana: わたしはもうくつはいてるよ。
lines.english: I've already got my shoes on, you know.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: 履いたよ。じゃあ、行こう。
lines.kana: はいたよ。じゃあ、いこう。
lines.english: There, they're on. Okay, let's go.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: え、ほんとだ。めっちゃ降ってる。
lines.kana: え、ほんとだ。めっちゃふってる。
lines.english: Oh, it has. It's really coming down.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, kaimono wa ashita ni shiyou ka.
lines.ja: じゃあ、買い物は明日にしようか。
lines.kana: じゃあ、かいものはあしたにしようか。
lines.english: Okay, shall we leave the shopping till tomorrow?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: ほんと？じゃあ、靴脱いでいい？
lines.kana: ほんと？じゃあ、くつぬいでいい？
lines.english: Really? Then can I take my shoes off?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.english: Sure. I'm taking mine off too.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: fuku mo nuide, mou ikkai neru.
lines.ja: 服も脱いで、もう一回寝る。
lines.kana: ふくもぬいで、もういっかいねる。
lines.english: I'm getting out of these clothes too and going back to bed.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, fuku mo nugu no? mou juuji da yo?
lines.ja: え、服も脱ぐの？もう十時だよ？
lines.kana: え、ふくもぬぐの？もうじゅうじだよ？
lines.english: What, your clothes too? It's ten o'clock!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenji! ame yanda yo! kaimono ikeru yo!
lines.ja: ケンジ！雨やんだよ！買い物行けるよ！
lines.kana: けんじ！あめやんだよ！かいものいけるよ！
lines.english: Kenji! The rain's stopped! We can go shopping!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, mou fuku mo kutsu mo nuijatta yo.
lines.ja: え、もう服も靴も脱いじゃったよ。
lines.kana: え、もうふくもくつもぬいじゃったよ。
lines.english: But I've already taken my clothes off. And my shoes.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, mou ikkai fuku kite, kutsu haite!
lines.ja: じゃあ、もう一回服着て、靴履いて！
lines.kana: じゃあ、もういっかいふくきて、くつはいて！
lines.english: Then put your clothes back on, and your shoes!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.kana: かいもの、あしたにしない？
lines.english: Can't we leave the shopping till tomorrow?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.kana: しない！じゅっぷんででるよ！
lines.english: No, we can't! We're leaving in ten minutes!

choices.english: Yuki and Kenji get caught in the rain on the way to the shops, so they come home and change out of their wet clothes.
Kenji takes too long getting dressed, so Yuki goes shopping without him and he goes back to bed.
Rain puts off the shopping, so Kenji gets undressed and goes back to bed; then the rain stops, and Yuki tells him to get dressed again.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-4: Kenji is dressed and puts his shoes on (kiteru yo / ima kutsu haku kara / haita yo). Line 5: it starts raining just as they're leaving (ame futte kita), and in line 7 Yuki puts the shopping off till tomorrow (ashita ni shiyou ka). Lines 8-12: shoes off, clothes off, back to bed (oyasumi). Line 13: the rain stops (ame yanda yo), and in line 15 Yuki tells him to get dressed again (mou ikkai fuku kite, kutsu haite!). A is wrong: they never leave the house, so nobody gets wet; the rain starts at the door (line 5). B is wrong: Kenji is ready in time (line 4: haita yo), and Yuki doesn't go without him: she wants him dressed again and out of the door in ten minutes (lines 15 and 17).

questions.english: Yuki calls out "fuku kita?" and Kenji answers "kiteru yo." What does he mean?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは今、どうですか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはいま、どうですか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa ima, dou desu ka?

choices.english: He has already come down and is waiting at the door.
His clothes are already on; the shoes are what he's doing now.
He's in the middle of getting dressed and will be done soon.

questions.explanation: Line 2: kiteru is a state, 'I have them on', not 'I'm putting them on now'. That's why he adds ima kutsu haku kara: shoes are the one thing left. C reads -teru like English '-ing', but with kiru, -teru means the clothes are already on. A hears kiteru as 'has come' (来てる): the same sounds, but that one falls after ki (KI-te-ru) while 'wearing' is flat (ki-TE-RU), and Yuki has just asked fuku kita? (did you get dressed?).

questions.english: You're dressed, but your shoes aren't on yet. Yuki calls from the front door: "mou deru yo! mada?" (We're leaving! Still not ready?) Tell her you're putting your shoes on now.
questions.answer: Say you're putting your shoes on now with haku: ima kutsu haku kara!

modelAnswers.english: I'm putting my shoes on now!

modelAnswers.romaji: fuku wa kiteru. ato wa kutsu haku dake.
modelAnswers.ja: 服は着てる。あとは靴履くだけ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm dressed. I just have to put my shoes on.

questions.explanation: Anything you step into goes on with haku, so shoes are kutsu o haku, never kutsu o kiru, even though English says 'wear' for both. Kenji does exactly this in line 2 (kiteru yo. ima kutsu haku kara): clothes with kiru, shoes with haku. Plain haku is 'putting them on now'; haiteru would mean they're already on, like Yuki's line 3 (watashi wa mou kutsu haiteru yo).

questions.english: When Yuki puts off the shopping, Kenji asks her something about his shoes. What did he ask?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Then can I take my shoes off?
Then can I pick up my shoes?
Then can I put my shoes on?

questions.explanation: Line 8: shoes come off with nugu, so Kenji asks kutsu nuide ii?, and Yuki answers watashi mo nugu (line 9: I'm taking mine off too). B is English 'take off' turned into toru: kutsu totte sounds like picking the shoes up or passing them to someone, not getting them off your feet. C is the opposite verb: haku puts shoes on, and Kenji already had his on (line 4: haita yo); with the shopping off, he wants them off.

questions.english: You come home soaked. Yuki says: "e, ame ni furareta no? kaze hiku yo!" (Oh, did you get caught in the rain? You'll catch a cold!) Tell her you'll get out of your clothes right away.
questions.ja: え、雨に降られたの？風邪ひくよ！
questions.kana: え、あめにふられたの？かぜひくよ！
questions.romaji: e, ame ni furareta no? kaze hiku yo!
questions.answer: Say you'll take your clothes off right away with nugu: un, sugu fuku nugu.

modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'll get out of these clothes right away.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、服脱いで、お風呂入る。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'll get these clothes off and have a bath.

questions.explanation: Whatever goes on with kiru or haku comes off with nugu, so clothes are fuku o nugu, as in Kenji's line 10 (fuku mo nuide, mou ikkai neru) and line 14 (mou fuku mo kutsu mo nuijatta yo). fuku o toru would sound like picking your clothes up (fuku totte = pass me my clothes). The same nugu took the shoes off in lines 8-9, so one verb undoes both kiru and haku.

newWords.english: decide on, go with (ashita ni shiyou = let's make it tomorrow)
take, pick up; pass (fuku totte = pass me my clothes)
